text: During a short break in a long trial. <break time="0.8s" /> The judges and lawyers of the Law Courts. <break time="0.8s" /> Gathered in a private room. <break time="0.8s" /> Where one of them opened a newspaper. <break time="0.8s" /> And read aloud that Ivan Ilyich Golovin had died. <break time="0.8s" /> Upon hearing the news. <break time="0.8s" /> Each man present thought first. <break time="0.8s" /> Not of the colleague he had lost. <break time="0.8s" /> But of the vacant post. <break time="0.8s" /> And of the promotions and transfers. <break time="0.8s" /> That it might bring. <break time="0.8s" /> To himself or to his friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Beneath these calculations. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay another feeling. <break time="0.8s" /> Which none of them would admit. <break time="0.8s" /> A quiet relief. <break time="0.8s" /> That the one. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had died at forty five. <break time="0.8s" /> Was Ivan Ilyich and not themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> His old friend Pyotr Ivanovich. <break time="0.8s" /> Went to the house that evening. <break time="0.8s" /> And although he had meant. <break time="0.8s" /> To share the familys grief. <break time="0.8s" /> He found himself thinking less. <break time="0.8s" /> About the dead man. <break time="0.8s" /> Than about the evenings card game. <break time="0.8s" /> In the drawing room. <break time="0.8s" /> The widow, Praskovya Fyodorovna. <break time="0.8s" /> Spoke at length. <break time="0.8s" /> Of her own suffering. <break time="0.8s" /> During her husbands illness. <break time="0.8s" /> And then asked, in the same tone. <break time="0.8s" /> How she might obtain. <break time="0.8s" /> More money from the government. <break time="0.8s" /> So absorbed was she. <break time="0.8s" /> In these practical matters. <break time="0.8s" /> That Pyotr Ivanovich. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting awkwardly. <break time="0.8s" /> On a low stool with broken springs. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to feel. <break time="0.8s" /> That his words of comfort were hardly needed. <break time="0.8s" /> As he was leaving. <break time="0.8s" /> He met Gerasim, the young servant. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had cared for his master to the end. <break time="0.8s" /> And Gerasim said simply. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was Gods will and that all of us must come to it one day. <break time="0.8s" /> Stepping out into the fresh night air. <break time="0.8s" /> Pyotr Ivanovich felt. <break time="0.8s" /> As if he had escaped something unpleasant. <break time="0.8s" /> And he hurried off. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping that he might still be in time for the card game.
